config.title: Build an accordion component

intro.title: Build an accordion component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive accordion component, a common UI pattern that allows users to expand and collapse sections of content. You will learn how to manage component state to track which sections are open or closed. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, event handling, and DOM manipulation to update the UI dynamically. By the end, you'll have a functional accordion that responds to user clicks, reinforcing fundamental concepts of state and interactivity in web development.
intro.usecase: Accordion components are essential UI patterns found across modern web applications. You'll see them in FAQ sections, product dashboards with collapsible panels, and settings menus where options are grouped by category. As a developer, you'll frequently implement accordions to manage information density while maintaining clean, accessible interfaces. They're particularly useful in admin panels, documentation sites, and mobile-first designs where screen space is limited.

objectives: Construct a reusable function to generate the HTML structure for an accordion component.
Initialize and manage the state of multiple accordion sections using JavaScript arrays and objects.
Implement click event handlers to toggle the visibility of individual accordion content panels.
Apply CSS classes dynamically to update the visual state of accordion headers and icons during interaction.
Configure the component to allow only one section to be open at a time (accordion behavior).
Integrate the accordion component into a webpage and render it with sample data.

import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.

steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

// Create the Accordion component here

steps.title: Initialize accordion data
steps.instruction: Inside your Accordion component, create a constant variable named 'accordionData' that holds an array of objects. Each object should have 'title' and 'content' properties with string values relevant to an accordion.
steps.hint: Define the array directly in the component body using const. Each object should look like { title: 'Your title', content: 'Your content' }.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an array of accordion items ready to be used for rendering.
successCriteria: The component contains a constant 'accordionData' variable with an array of objects, each having 'title' and 'content' string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure 'accordionData' is an array of objects, each with both 'title' and 'content' as strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data structure isn't quite right. Create an array of objects with 'title' and 'content' properties inside your component.

steps.title: Initialize state for open items
steps.instruction: Inside your Accordion component, use the useState hook to declare a state variable named 'openIndexes' initialized as an empty array [].
steps.hint: Call useState with [] as the initial value and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a list of items
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable to track which accordion items are open.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with [] and destructured into 'openIndexes' and 'setOpenIndexes' variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with [] and destructuring into 'openIndexes' and 'setOpenIndexes'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use useState([]) to create state for tracking open items.

steps.title: Add container structure
steps.instruction: Inside your Accordion component, return a div container element from the component.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div element that will wrap your accordion content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div container element instead of null.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element
The return statement is properly structured with parentheses
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element from the component. Check that you've replaced 'null' with a proper JSX div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element. Look at the analogous example to see how to structure the return statement.

steps.title: Add item header with title
steps.instruction: Inside the map callback, create a <div> element that will serve as the clickable header for each accordion item. This div should display the item's title and have an onClick handler that calls the toggleItem function with the current index.
steps.hint: Remember to pass the current index to toggleItem when the header is clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each accordion item will have a clickable header that displays its title and toggles its open/closed state when clicked.
successCriteria: The map callback returns a <div> element with an onClick handler that calls toggleItem(index) and displays {item.title}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the header div has an onClick handler that calls toggleItem with the current index and displays the item's title.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header isn't quite right. Check that you've added a <div> with onClick={...} that calls toggleItem(index) and shows {item.title}.

steps.title: Add content section
steps.instruction: Inside the map callback, after the header div, add a content div that conditionally renders the item's content only when that item's index is in the openIndexes array.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to check if openIndexes.includes(index). If true, render a div with the content text. If false, render nothing (null).
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion will have content sections that appear only when their corresponding header is clicked (open).
successCriteria: A content div is added inside the map callback that uses a ternary operator to conditionally render item.content based on whether openIndexes includes the current index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your conditional rendering. Make sure you're using a ternary operator that checks if openIndexes.includes(index) and renders the content div when true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The content section isn't properly conditionally rendered. Remember to add a div after the header that only shows item.content when that item's index is in the openIndexes array.

steps.title: Add basic styling and test
steps.instruction: Add a content div inside the map that conditionally renders when the current index is in openIndexes, and add basic CSS styles to the accordion container, headers, and content sections.
steps.hint: Use a conditional check with openIndexes.includes(index) to determine if content should be shown. Add className attributes with CSS classes for styling.
steps.expectedOutcome: The accordion will have visual styling and clicking headers will toggle content visibility with smooth expansion/collapse.
successCriteria: Content sections conditionally render based on openIndexes state, and CSS classes are applied to accordion container, items, headers, and content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the conditional content rendering and the CSS classNames for styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the conditional content div and applied CSS classes to all accordion elements.
